answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making trust accrue with age, not headcount. Every new identity starts weightless; voting power grows only after long, unbroken stretches of peer-attested uptime, like a beacon that must burn through a cold tundra night before others rely on its light. An attacker who spawns a thousand fresh clones gains a thousand weightless accounts, each forced through the same slow aging, so influence cannot be bought in bulk. The cost is months of patient waiting and upkeep, while genuine agents quietly build standing in the shared meadow.
